correctness.rationale: At \(\mathcal R_0=1\), the source's linear Lyapunov function has the exact derivative \(\dot V=-\mu_AAS/(K+S)\), whose largest invariant zero set is the origin, proving global convergence and stability. At the same threshold the Jacobian has one simple zero root and a Hurwitz cubic factor. With normalized positive left/right zero eigenvectors, the exact critical coordinate satisfies \(\dot z=-AS/[H(K+S)]\). Positivity makes the full state comparable to \(z\); exponential stability of the complementary spectral subspace then gives \(x=zr+o(z)\), hence \(\dot z=-(C/(KH))z^2(1+o(1))\) and the stated \(t^{-1}\) limit. The packaged exact-rational checker verifies all displayed normalization identities and a concrete threshold witness. The computation is supportive; the generic proof is analytic.

value.rationale: The equality case is the management boundary singled out by the source. Showing that extinction remains globally asymptotically stable at exactly \(\mathcal R_0=1\), while slowing from exponential to the explicit \(t^{-1}\) law, changes the mathematical interpretation of the threshold and quantifies critical slowing in every biological stage. The result is structural rather than a parameter-table recomputation: it combines a global invariant-set closure with a universal asymptotic profile for all nonzero nonnegative initial data.
